source.title: Evaluating Open-Source LLMs for Multi-Label ATT&CK Technique Classification on CTI Reports
source.authors: A. Ryan; Saad Sakib Noor; Md Erfan; Shaswata Mitra; Sudip Mittal; Md. Rayhanur Rahman

record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream classification performance across model sizes and reports a size-performance correlation, using task F1 rather than pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The study tests downstream task performance versus parameter size (V6). It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit scaling power laws, test extrapolation from smaller runs, or examine compute-optimal allocations. The RAG comparison is between different models and configurations, so it does not isolate a size or scaling effect.
record.test_reason: The study compares seven existing open models (8B–236B, different families) on one new downstream task, CTI multi-label ATT&CK classification. It reports a rank correlation between parameter count and micro F1. That bears weakly on V6 in a new setting. Model family, architecture (MoE vs dense) and training differ across sizes, and no scaling fit or prediction is made, so this is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find parameter size the only statistically significant predictor of F1, with non-monotonic exceptions. They also find prompt strategy, CoT and temperature have no significant effect. They argue that closing the gap needs external knowledge (RAG) and domain-specific training, not prompt tuning, and that current open models are insufficient for production use.
record.recipe_differences: This evaluates downstream multi-label CTI classification F1 across existing models, rather than training model and data sweeps and measuring held-out pretraining loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Model architecture and training factors affect the size-performance relationship; the 70B model outperformed the 120B model, and the 20B model was a marked outlier.
record.problems: The evaluation uses one CTI dataset and one downstream classification task; all models use Q4_K_M 4-bit quantization. Model architecture and training are not held constant across sizes, and the authors note confounding between model size and other factors. The reported model-level means aggregate eight configurations each.
record.rows_left_out: The RAG result in Table V was not extracted as a row because it compares a RAG-enabled 70B model with a different, non-RAG 236B model and does not isolate a scale effect.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss measured; no training sweeps.
No fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No other modalities or training regimes.
No relation to pretraining loss and no fitted or predictive form. Only one task, all models 4-bit quantized, and sizes span different model families rather than a controlled series.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices examined.

missing.what: Spearman rank correlation between parameter size and F1 (ρ=0.85, p=0.014). This is the study's main V6 result and has no row. It is unclear whether it was computed on 7 model means or on all 53 configurations.
missing.locator: Section V-C1, Table VIII note; Section VIII

missing.what: Macro F1 per model, which gives a different ranking: LLM70 0.15, DS236 0.14, GP120 0.13, GMM27 0.12, GMM12 0.11, LLM08 0.10, GPT20 0.03.
CoT raised micro F1 by 0.02–0.05 only for DS236 and LLM70 (the largest models), with negligible or negative change for the other five.

record.verdict_notes: This is weak evidence for V6. It has seven heterogeneous models, size confounded with family and architecture (MoE vs dense), one task, 4-bit quantization, and no loss measurement or fitted law. It shows ordinal association, not predictability. The Table VIII note says each mean aggregates 8 configurations, but Table IV omits three (two for LLM70, one for LLM08). The reported p-value matches a 7-point Spearman test with ρ≈0.857, despite the note that tests used all 53 configurations. The RAG comparison is correctly left out. It does not isolate scale, and the authors acknowledge the confound.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Predicting larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations as compute changes.
Architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
Scaling laws in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures one downstream CTI classification task using F1; it does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or across other task types.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures of loss curves from power laws.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-V2.5
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean micro F1 across models of different parameter sizes; each mean aggregates 8 inference configurations.
rows.note: The study identifies this as the maximum mean F1 across the tested models.
rows.check: No row-level problem. Note that individual model means only bear on V6 jointly; the key evidence is the cross-model Spearman correlation, which no row records.

rows.subject: GPT-OSS
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean micro F1 across models of different parameter sizes; each mean aggregates 8 inference configurations.
rows.note: The 120B model scored below the 70B Llama model, so performance did not increase monotonically with stated size.
rows.check: A single model's mean cannot by itself show a scale trend. Read against neighbours, GP120 (0.18) sits above 27B (0.17) but below the smaller 70B model (0.19). The size–performance ordering is therefore only partly respected, a small inversion.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean micro F1 across models of different parameter sizes; each mean aggregates 8 inference configurations.
rows.note: The study explicitly notes that this 70B model outperformed the larger 120B model.
rows.check: The aggregation condition is wrong. Table IV lists only 6 LLM70 configurations (two omitted), not 8, although the Table VIII note claims 8 per model.

rows.subject: Gemma 3
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean micro F1 across models of different parameter sizes; each mean aggregates 8 inference configurations.
rows.note: The table identifies the model as GMM27; the model name and size are given in Table I.
rows.check: No row-level problem; this is one point in a cross-family comparison.

rows.subject: GPT-OSS
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean micro F1 across models of different parameter sizes; each mean aggregates 8 inference configurations.
rows.note: The authors describe this model's performance deficit as showing that architectural or training factors can override parameter size.
rows.check: GPT20 (20B) scores 0.02, below both smaller models (12B: 0.13, 8B: 0.09). It is a clear reversal of the size ordering, not merely partial.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 Instruct

relationships.condition: Across the seven open models on sentence-level CTI ATT&CK classification (4-bit quantized)
relationships.reason: Mean micro F1 rises broadly with parameter count (r1, r3, r4, r6, r7). The authors report Spearman ρ=0.85, p=0.014; this is from the text, as no row records it.
relationships.display_finding: Mean micro F1 generally increased with model size, with Spearman ρ=0.85 and p=0.014.

relationships.condition: When size is compared across different model families and architectures
relationships.reason: The trend is non-monotonic. GP120 (0.18) is below LLM70 (0.19) (r2, r3), and GPT20 at 20B (0.02) is below the 12B and 8B models (r5). The authors say training or architecture can override size.
relationships.display_finding: GP120 scored 0.18 versus LLM70's 0.19, while GPT20 at 20B scored 0.02 and underperformed 12B and 8B models, indicating that training or architecture could outweigh size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Across the seven tested models on the CTI classification task
reader_labels.reason: Parameter size had a statistically significant positive correlation with F1 (ρ = 0.85, p = 0.014); rows r1–r7 report the model-level mean scores.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Comparisons across model architectures and training configurations
reader_labels.reason: The relationship was not monotonic: the 70B model scored above the 120B model, and the 20B model had a particularly low score; the authors note that architecture or training factors can override size (rows r2, r3, r5).
